outcome: late pregnancy loss (>=13 and <20 weeks gestation)
cohort: The study included 79,416 autologous frozen-thaw embryo transfer (FET) cycles with the transfer of single genetically tested embryos, excluding cycles associated with recurrent pregnancy loss, gestational carrier, donor egg, or donor embryo.
finding: Maternal race and ethnicity are associated with significant disparities in pregnancy outcomes after single genetically tested frozen-thaw embryo transfer, with non-Hispanic Black, Asian, Hispanic, and other minority women experiencing higher rates of preterm birth and lower rates of live birth compared to non-Hispanic White women.
mod_finding: The likelihood of delivery by Cesarean section was disproportionately higher in non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic women, and those identifying with more than one race compared to non-Hispanic White women.
